title: Emrys and the Letter
premise: In 1747, in a river town on the edge of the Habsburg frontier, Ivo Fairweather — an apprentice of no family and no name worth recording — completes the atlas their dying master smuggled out of imperial archives: maps that prove the crown has been redrawing borders to erase three villages from existence. When winter closes the bridge and imperial inspectors arrive hunting the missing documents, Ivo must hide in plain sight among the townspeople who slowly claim them as one of their own. Guided by Marta, a ferryman's widow with her own reasons to hate the crown, and pursued by an inspector who once loved Ivo's master, they carry the atlas's hidden plates downriver through three checkpoints. The final crossing costs them nearly everything — but the evidence reaches the cartographers' guild in Vienna, and Ivo, who measured the world in what could be carried, finally learns that some things are carried by holding still.
about_author: Freya Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing disputed border surveys in Central European collections. She writes historical fiction about the people history forgot to record, and lives near a river she has never successfully mapped.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Ivo Fairweather, POV. In the cold workshop, Ivo finishes inking the last plate of Master Aldous's forbidden atlas while the old man dies upstairs, whispering about what the maps prove. Ivo measures their life in portable things and realizes the atlas cannot be carried anywhere safely. Emotional beat: grief braided with dread — inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. The ferryman's widow buries her husband and notices the apprentice watching the bridge too carefully. She offers Ivo work mending nets, less kindness than reconnaissance — she knows Aldous was hiding something. Emotional beat: two guarded people circling each other, each mistaking caution for indifference.

chapters.title: Orders Come with the Frost
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Imperial writs arrive: the bridge closes for the season, inspectors are coming, and all papers in town will be examined. Ivo hides the atlas plates inside a broken surveyor's case and lies for the first time in their life. Emotional beat: the sick clarity of realizing invisibility was always someone else's permission.

chapters.title: Three Villages, Erased
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Reading Aldous's marginalia fully for the first time, Ivo understands the maps show the crown redrawing the border to erase three villages — including the one Marta's husband came from. They bring this to Marta, breaking their silence. Emotional beat: guilt transmuting into purpose; the found-family thread begins.

chapters.title: The Inspector's Patience
chapters.summary: Inspector Voss, POV. A courteous, dangerous man who knew Aldous in Vienna, Voss arrives and begins methodically interviewing the town, charming secrets loose. He interviews Ivo last and lingers, sensing a familiar hand in the atlas's style. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse where the mouse admires the cat.

chapters.title: Nets and Names
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. The town quietly folds Ivo into its rituals — a shared table, a borrowed coat, a name spoken without 'the apprentice.' Marta teaches Ivo the river's winter moods and reveals her village was one of the erased three. Emotional beat: belonging arriving sideways, unasked for, undeniable.

chapters.title: The First Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. With the ice thickening, Ivo and Marta move the plates downriver by night skiff to a sympathetic miller — checkpoint one passed, but Voss finds Aldous's empty strongbox and stops pretending courtesy. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into terror; no way back now.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Mill
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. The miller's son sells them out; soldiers seize the decoy case while the real plates ride inside a coffin bound for the churchyard. Voss confronts Ivo directly, offering absolution in exchange for the master's confession. Emotional beat: the cost of trust, and the discovery that some betrayals can be survived.

chapters.title: The Last Crossing
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. At the frozen third checkpoint, Voss corners them — but chooses, in one unguarded moment, to look away, honoring a debt to Aldous he never admitted. Ivo passes the plates to a guild courier as the ice cracks. Emotional beat: climax; mercy from an enemy, courage from a person who thought themselves a ghost.

chapters.title: A Map of Staying
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV, spring. News reaches the town: the guild has published the true borders; the villages are being restored to the record. Ivo declines Vienna's offer and stays, drawing a new map — of the town, its people, their names — as Marta sets a second plate at the table. Emotional beat: resolution; identity not carried but built, love chosen over duty fulfilled.
